clue.text: United Nations' communication invalidating Iran's flag

indicators.note: invalidating suggests making something unsound or broken, so these letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: the possessive S is kept as a letter here
taken as written

explanation.surface: A diplomatic message from the UN declares Iran's national flag invalid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invalidating' tells you to rearrange IRANS + FLAG. The definition is playful: the mixed language belongs to two united nations, France and England, rather than to the UN.
explanation.definitionFit: A hybrid tongue of French laced with English words is a communication shared by two nations joined together.

clue.text: Muscle is twisted, unused

indicators.note: twisted means the little word is turned round so it reads backwards

parts.note: taken as written before turning
something unused is new

explanation.surface: A muscle has been wrenched and so goes unused.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendon or piece of muscular tissue is loosely called this, a synonym for brawn or muscle.

clue.text: Passionate figures: slightly smaller one outside, scratching head

indicators.note: outside says the trimmed number goes round the other piece
scratching off the head means the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: nine is a figure just slightly smaller than ten, following on from figures as tens
tens are figures or numbers

explanation.surface: A heated figure-skating judgement about a smaller rival scratching its head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slightly smaller one' leans on 'figures' read as TENS: one slightly smaller is NINE. 'scratching head' removes its N to leave INE, which goes 'outside' TENS.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense feelings are strong and fervent, the same as passionate ones.

clue.text: Conservative drubbing happening, one in the soup?

parts.note: a drubbing is a rout, a heavy defeat
something happening is on

explanation.surface: Tories taking a beating at the polls: are they now in the soup?
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the soup' suggests being in trouble, following the Conservative defeat, but it is literal: a crouton floats in soup.
explanation.definitionFit: A small cube of fried bread is something served floating in a bowl of soup.

clue.text: OK, man

definitions.meaning: radio jargon for message received and understood
a man's name, as in the boy's name

explanation.definitionFit: Radio operators say this word for agreed, and it is also a common male name.

clue.text: Large, leather bands

definitions.meaning: big and powerfully built, as a hefty youth
straps collectively, strips of leather used for fastening

explanation.definitionFit: The word means sturdy and well built, and also material made of leather straps.

clue.text: A bit rowdy at first during party

indicators.note: during says one letter falls within the span of the other word

parts.note: a faction is a party or group within a larger body

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A party gets a little rowdy at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A fraction is a small part or portion of something, a bit of it.

clue.text: Question and answer stopping instruction

parts.note: who is a question word

explanation.surface: A question and answer session on how to stop.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the call to a horse to halt, so an instruction to stop.

clue.text: Bouncer in a legendary maiden?

definitions.meaning: a sound that bounces back off a surface
the nymph in Greek myth who pined for Narcissus until only her voice was left

explanation.definitionFit: The reflected sound bounces back, and the Greek nymph of myth bears the same name.

clue.text: Allies importing revolutionary weapons

indicators.note: importing means taking something inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: mates are allies or friends
Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary

explanation.surface: Allied forces bring in arms for revolutionaries.
explanation.walkthrough: CHE is Che Guevara, the Argentine-born revolutionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Machetes are large broad-bladed knives, which can be used as weapons.

clue.text: Unfortunately, pro team stuffed by America — hard cheese?

indicators.note: stuffed by says the other piece is packed into the middle of this one
unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: US is America

explanation.surface: A professional side beaten by the Americans: hard cheese, chaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfortunately' rearranges PRO TEAM to MOETRAP, and US goes inside it. 'Hard cheese' looks like the British idiom for bad luck; in fact mousetrap is British slang for cheap hard Cheddar.
explanation.definitionFit: Mousetrap is British slang for ordinary low-quality hard cheese such as Cheddar.

clue.text: In fashion, new cooker

indicators.note: in says the short piece sits inside the longer one

parts.note: the rage is the current fashion

explanation.surface: A new cooker is the height of fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English a range is a large kitchen stove.
explanation.definitionFit: A range is a large cooking stove with ovens and hotplates.

clue.text: Position when losing tennis match?

definitions.meaning: to place or put something somewhere
a player trailing by a set is one set behind

explanation.definitionFit: To place something is to put it down, and a tennis player behind by a set is one set down.

clue.text: Frozen item, best to keep cold

indicators.note: to keep means holding the other letter within

parts.note: choice means best, as in choice cuts
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Advice that a frozen item is best stored cold.
explanation.walkthrough: A choc ice is a British ice cream bar coated in chocolate.
explanation.definitionFit: This British treat is a block of ice cream with a chocolate coating, eaten frozen.

clue.text: Bottle that may be attached to optic?

definitions.text: that may be attached to optic?
definitions.meaning: the optic one links the eye to the brain

explanation.definitionFit: Courage, called bottle in British slang, and also the fibre linking the eye to the brain.

clue.text: Squeezing belly, minor gets attention

indicators.note: squeezing says one piece is pressed inside the other

parts.note: slight means minor or small
a pot is a pot belly, a paunch

explanation.surface: A child pressing their tummy is seeking attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the public eye or the centre of notice is being in the spotlight.

clue.text: Brother, one boiling in oil, say?

indicators.note: say indicates the word is to be pronounced, sounding like another

parts.note: a fryer is something that cooks food in boiling oil

explanation.surface: A monk being boiled in oil, perhaps as a martyr.
explanation.definitionFit: A friar is a member of a religious order, addressed as Brother.

clue.text: The group A-ha turn nasty, one of those producing an album?

definitions.text: one of those producing an album?

indicators.note: nasty means turning ugly, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the band's name without its hyphen

explanation.surface: The Norwegian pop band a-ha turn nasty with a fan wanting an album signed.
explanation.walkthrough: A-ha were a Norwegian pop group of the 1980s. 'nasty' rearranges THE GROUP AHA TURN.
explanation.definitionFit: A collector who asks celebrities to sign an album fills it with signatures.

clue.text: On summit of Everest, man welcomes time to create

indicators.note: in a down clue on places one piece after another
welcomes means taking a guest inside, so one word holds the other

parts.note: a gent is a man
an era is a period of time

indicators.note: summit means the top, here the first letter of the mountain's name

explanation.surface: A climber on top of Everest receives a time to create something.
explanation.definitionFit: To generate is to produce or bring into being, the same as create.

clue.text: A portrayal in horror

parts.note: a version is one account or portrayal of something

explanation.surface: A depiction of a horror film.
explanation.definitionFit: An aversion is a strong dislike, a feeling of horror towards something.

clue.text: Dry river becoming land

parts.note: sec is dry, of wine
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A river drying up and turning into land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'land' is a verb here, as in to land or secure a contract. The Ure is a river in North Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: To secure a deal is to land it, obtain it successfully.

clue.text: Wet blankets left wet

indicators.note: blankets is a verb, covering, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: soppy means wet, feeble or sentimental

explanation.surface: Wet blankets left out in the rain are soaked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wet blankets' looks like the phrase for killjoys; 'blankets' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloppy ground or food is wet and slushy.

clue.text: A wise man evidently rising, protecting hospital yet

indicators.note: protecting means guarding by surrounding, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: a wise man is plainly no twit, no fool
standing up is rising

explanation.surface: A sage rising to his feet, guarding a hospital anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'A wise man evidently' as NO TWIT, a cryptic description; H sits between it and STANDING.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means nevertheless or in spite of that, the same as yet.

clue.text: Arm around English girl, one holding a drink

indicators.note: around says one piece encloses the letter

parts.note: a wing is an arm of a building or organisation
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A man putting his arm round an English girl who holds a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A stemmed glass made for serving wine is something that holds a drink.

clue.text: Fearsome arcane clan's ultimate secret society member

indicators.note: arcane means mysterious and obscure, so the letters are rearranged
ultimate means the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A fearsome, mysterious clan's final secret, as kept by a lodge member.
explanation.definitionFit: A Freemason belongs to a fraternal order known for its secret rituals.

clue.text: Briefly look: chap stirring duck soup

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, losing the final letter

parts.note: to gaze is to look

indicators.note: stirring mixes these letters into a new order

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of zero, O

explanation.surface: Glance quickly: a man stirring duck soup.
explanation.definitionFit: Gazpacho is a cold Spanish soup of tomatoes and vegetables.

clue.text: Nation not entirely upset, supporting cleaner carbon fuel

indicators.note: in a down clue supporting means placed below the other pieces

parts.note: a char is a cleaning lady in British usage
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the letters upside down, reading upwards
not entirely means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: Laos is a nation in Southeast Asia

explanation.surface: A nation in turmoil props up a coal-cleaning business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns LAO (Laos without S, from 'not entirely') into OAL. A char, or charwoman, is a British cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: Charcoal is a carbon-rich fuel made by burning wood without air.

clue.text: Cold water made warm to heat the feet

indicators.note: the feet of words are their bottom ends, so the last letter of each is taken

explanation.surface: Cold water warmed to heat up chilly feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feet' signals the final letter of each of the six words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Remote can mean aloof and unfriendly, as a cold manner is.

clue.text: Leader of union controlled powerful nation, becoming a God

indicators.note: leader of means the first letter of the word

parts.note: ran means controlled, as one runs a firm
the US is a superpower

explanation.surface: A union boss ran a mighty nation and was deified.
explanation.definitionFit: Uranus was the Greek god of the sky, father of the Titans.

clue.text: Use final bits of underwater equipment beneath river

indicators.note: in a down clue beneath means the letters come after

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon

indicators.note: the final bits are the last letters of each of the two words

explanation.surface: Using diving gear in the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exe is a river in Devon in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: To exert strength is to apply or use it.
